thread:
maria: Heads-up — during a spike last night the OTLP proxy started marking backends unhealthy and we saw ~30% of spans dropped. Need a quick sync on healthchecks/backoff/timeouts.
kev: saw that too. Proxy logs show repeated TLS handshakes and HTTP/2 resets. suspect connection churn + aggressive probe settings.
sylvia: can you paste the probe lines?
maria: log snippet:
```
2026-03-17T23:41:02Z proxy healthcheck failed: EOF
2026-03-17T23:41:02Z backend 10.2.3.7:4317 state->unhealthy (consecutive_failures=5)
2026-03-17T23:41:03Z grpc: stream error: code=Unavailable desc=\"transport is closing\"
```
lee: hmm. We set healthcheck interval to 2s and failure threshold 3 to fail fast for rollout. That might be too aggressive under bursty attach/detach.
maria: right — but we also have client-side deadlines set to 1s for span exporter. Combined -> clients give up, proxy sees lots of aborted streams, marks backend repeatedly.
kev: idea: introduce a short \"probe backoff\" that uses exponential backoff for marking healthy/unhealthy during high churn windows. Keep fast detection for normal ops.
sylvia: also consider moving healthchecks to a lightweight TCP probe instead of full gRPC call. Current gRPC probe establishes stream and costs more under TLS.
lee: TCP probes won't validate ALPN / HTTP2 though, could miss protocol-level failures. Maybe do TCP for failing-fast and every Nth probe do a full gRPC healthcheck.
maria: agree. Also want to tweak exporter retry/backoff so we don't hammer proxy during outages. Current client backoff: initial=50ms, multiplier=1.5, max=500ms. Clients retry up to 5 times.
kev: that's small. For spans batching, retries should be sparse — else we flood when proxy is slow. Proposal: initial=200ms, multiplier=2, max=5s, max_retries=3.
sylvia: +1. Also add jitter to avoid thundering herd. Use full jitter.
lee: we also need an early-degrade path: if proxy queue length > 5000, drop non-critical spans (sampling) and return success to clients with metadata so they know.
maria: okay but that requires producers to understand 202-info header; infra change.
kev: we can use response header X-Redwood-Span-Accept: partial or full. If partial, client can backoff sampling rate.
sylvia: config snippet for proxy healthchecks proposal:
```
healthcheck:
  interval_seconds: 5
  timeout_seconds: 2
  failure_threshold: 5
  probe_type: hybrid # tcp-first, full-grpc-every-5
  degraded_backoff_seconds: 30
```
maria: and exporter retry config for SDKs:
```
otlp_exporter:
  transport: auto # prefer http when payload < 1MB, grpc otherwise
  retries:
    initial_ms: 200
    multiplier: 2.0
    max_ms: 5000
    max_attempts: 3
    jitter: full
  timeout_ms: 8000
```
lee: note on transport: HTTP/1.1 + keepalive works for small bursts and is simpler through proxies. But for large payloads or streaming KV cache we should use gRPC.
kev: ops ask for a per-route timeout override from Console so SREs can quickly relax thresholds during incidents. Any objections?
sylvia: no objections. But make sure rollouts of the new probe config are gradual (canary 1%, then 10%). Healthcheck changes can introduce flapping if mis-tuned.
maria: agreed. Plan of action:
- sylvia: implement hybrid probe in proxy by EOD Tuesday
- kev: update SDK default retry params + add opt-in header X-Redwood-Span-Accept behavior
- lee: add Console toggle for per-route health/timeout overrides
- ops: I'll coordinate a canary rollout and smoke tests

ops: @maria noted. will set up a canary cluster and alert rule: if proxy backend_unhealthy_count increases > 3/min during rollout, auto-rollback.
kev: I'll open a PR for SDKs with test harness + perf numbers.
sylvia: will add unit tests and a simulation tool to replay TLS handshakes/resets to tune thresholds.
maria: thanks. If anyone sees additional spikes tonight drop a note here with logs. :thumbsup:
note-bot: Incident detector: detected 3 burst spikes in OTLP ingestion between 23:30-00:15 UTC, linked runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/otlp-burst
maria: linking runbook in case folks need it. https://redwood.internal/runbooks/otlp-burst
lee: also let's add telemetry: counters for probe_type, probe_latency_ms, exporter_retry_count, exporter_backoff_ms, sampling_drops_total. That gives us visibility.
kev: added to my PR checklist.
maria: cool — thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after the canary starts.
